alignments.note: Accusative demonstrative object of the participle, rendered adverbially as *thus*. It stands inside the participial clause's English but is its own unit: rule 15 forbids absorbing it into s003 merely because that unit is discontinuous around it.
Inferential conjunction. *therefore* stands inside the participial clause, which is where οὖν stands in the Greek; the second particle ἄρα belongs to the following interrogative clause.

Participle recast as a finite temporal clause. The supplied *When* is a rule 7 helper, not `added`: rule 86's test is whether a source token licenses the subordination, and a participle does — the corpus places a supplied *when* on a participle in sixty-six of its sixty-seven units. Subject *I* and copula *was* ride along under rules 7 and 9; head on the lexical *minded* under rule 17. Discontinuous around t005 under rule 15.

Interrogative particle whose only work is to mark the question. The ASV marks it by inversion and supplies no interrogative word, so rules 44 and 64 leave it empty. The *did* of *did I show* is the past indicative's own do-support riding with s008 under rule 9, exactly as the auxiliary does in rule 44's `μὴ πλείονα σημεῖα ποιήσει;` → *will he do more signs?*; it is not a supplied interrogative word of rule 64's `μήτι` → *Can* kind. A reference comparison will report this as a disagreement, and that report is not a correction.

Second particle in the interrogative frame, likewise unwritten in the ASV; rule 64. Raised from `medium`: the only materially different reading is giving *therefore* to ἄρα and emptying οὖν, and clause position excludes it, *therefore* standing in the participial clause where οὖν stands while ἄρα stands in the following clause. No *then* is written anywhere in the verse, so rule 16 leaves no competing analysis to hedge against and rule 84's line against hedging an undisputed unit applies. A reference comparison will report this as a disagreement, and that report is not a correction.

The ASV gives *fickleness* no determiner, so the article has no *the* to anchor and is `unrepresented` under rule 23; the dative is absorbed into the English object of *show*, and rule 21 forbids leaving a bare case preposition on the article.
Noun complement of χράομαι, spelled out as *fickleness*. Rule 73 does not join it to s008: the ASV writes both elements of the pair, so rule 2's ordinary split applies.
Finite verb with the inverted do-support *did* and subject *I* as rule 9 helpers; head on the lexical *show* under rule 17.
Disjunctive particle.

Relative pronoun substantivized with the supplied generic noun *things*. Rule 77's generic-noun arm heads such a unit on *things* rather than on the relativizer, as `ἃ εἰργασάμεθα` → *the things which we have wrought* does; the determiner and relativizer are rule 7 helpers.
Verb of the relative clause, with subject *I* as a rule 9 helper; head on the lexical verb.
Preposition rendered by the contiguous two-word *according to*, headed on *according*. Rule 67 is not in question: no supplied noun makes this a complex frame.
`κατὰ σάρκα` is anarthrous, so no article competes for the determiner slot and the supplied *the* is an ordinary rule 7 helper on the noun it determines, as rule 51 has it. Head on *flesh*.
Repeated finite verb heading the main interrogative clause, with do-support *do* and subject *I* as rule 9 helpers; head on *purpose*.
Purpose conjunction realized by the word introducing its English clause, *that*; rule 40.
Subjunctive of εἰμί with the expletive *there* and modal *should* as rule 9 helpers; head on the lexical *be*.
Preposition realized by *with*. Rule 94's precondition for a compound unit is not met: the ASV writes two separate English words, so rule 2 splits the phrase.
Dative pronoun.

Article nominalizing the quoted particle, realized by the written *the*; rule 19. Rule 61's `unrepresented` nominalizer does not reach it, that rule aligning the article wherever the ASV writes a determiner of its own.
First quoted *yea*.
Second quoted *yea*, kept its own unit under rule 2.
Coordinating conjunction.
Article nominalizing the quoted negative, realized by the written *the*; rule 19.
First quoted *nay*.
Second quoted *nay*. The doubled negatives are quoted words rather than an emphatic negation, and they are not the adjacent `οὐ μή` pair, so rule 33 is not in question and rule 2 splits them.

review_notes: All 25 source and all 36 target IDs are partitioned exactly once; every aligned unit's head is a member of its own array.

Changed from the accepted alignment: s005 `ἄρα` raised from `medium` to `high`. The accepted note conceded that no *then* stands in the verse, which defeats its own hedge. The only materially different reading is giving *therefore* to ἄρα and leaving οὖν empty, and clause position excludes it — *therefore* sits in the participial clause where οὖν stands. Rule 16 wants a competing analysis, and rule 84 warns that hedging against an undisputed unit is the recurring failure. Everything else is unchanged.

s004 and s005 are separate `unrepresented` units under rules 44 and 64. The point worth recording is that *did* is not a supplied interrogative word: it is the past indicative's do-support required by English inversion, so it rides with s008 under rule 9, as the auxiliary does in rule 44's `μὴ πλείονα σημεῖα ποιήσει;` → *will he do more signs?*. Rule 64's `μήτι` → *Can* case is the contrast, where the supplied modal carries a sense the Greek verb does not. A reference comparison will report both particles as disagreements, and that report is not a correction.

s003's *When* is a rule 7 helper on the participle, not `added`. Rule 86's test is whether a source token licenses the subordination, and a participle is exactly such a token; the corpus places a supplied *when* on a participle in sixty-six of its sixty-seven units.

s007/s008 are split rather than joined: `τῇ ἐλαφρίᾳ ἐχρησάμην` → *did I show fickleness* spells both elements out, so rule 73's collapsed light-verb pair is not in question and rule 2's ordinary split applies.

s006 is `unrepresented` because the ASV writes no determiner for *fickleness*; rule 21 forbids leaving a bare case preposition on the article. Contrast s013, where the Greek is anarthrous and the supplied *the* is therefore the noun's own helper under rule 51, and s019/s023, where the ASV writes *the* and rules 19 and 61 align the article to it.
s010 heads on *things* per rule 77's generic-noun arm, not on the relativizer *that*.
The doubled `ναί ναί` and `οὔ οὔ` are quoted particles, each its own unit under rule 2; rule 33 is not in question, these being neither adjacent `οὐ μή` nor an emphatic negation.
